The Tower of Science maps how ideas buil: The Tower of Science maps how ideas build on, challenge, and transform one another. It is a curated guide to scientific development, not a complete family tree of human knowledge.
Earlier milestones sit lower; later ones: Earlier milestones sit lower; later ones sit higher. Approximate contemporaries share period floors, with exact dates preserved in the index. Cards are centered within their subbranch cells. Science sections reserve separate horizontal regions within each era and expand to accommodate their busiest floor. The shape stays fixed when filtering. At far zoom, inactive branches become named summaries within their eras. Labels retain a readable size and may shift to avoid collisions; the underlying concept positions do not move. Selecting a branch name reveals its concepts while keeping your current selection and filters. Summary connections group the same cited relationships and do not create new historical claims. Time is compressed, and spacing is not a measure of importance or difficulty. Multiple roots acknowledge that counting, observation, craft, and practical knowledge arose in many communities. Unrecorded contributions cannot be reconstructed with certainty.
Documented connections are supported by: Documented connections are supported by the cited accounts. Conceptual connections are editorial interpretations of prerequisites, not evidence of historical transmission. Contested links identify uncertainty. The graph represents development without claiming that history was inevitable.
Modern branches are navigational categor: Modern branches are navigational categories applied retrospectively, not claims about how historical communities divided knowledge. Each idea has one primary location; related branches identify interdisciplinary associations. Empty periods are omitted. Floors span prehistory, 500 years from 5000–500 BCE, 100 years to 1500, 25 years to 1850, 10 years to 1900, and five years afterward, split at era boundaries.
Bundled mode groups existing connections: Bundled mode groups existing connections by section (or subbranch at closer zoom), era pair, relationship type, and evidence classification. Counts include distinct relationships after filters. Selected ideas show their immediate connections individually. Open a bundle to inspect its complete evidence or expand its members. Focus only hides background links; All connections draws each relationship. Bundles do not affect ancestry, pillar counts, or scientific standing.
A pillar has five or more distinct, supp: A pillar has five or more distinct, supported direct descendants in this edition. Documented and explicitly identified conceptual links count; contested links do not. Total descendants include indirect paths, counted once per concept. These are properties of this collection, not universal rankings of scientific value.
Dates usually identify a publication, fo: Dates usually identify a publication, formulation, observation, or surviving record. Approximate dates and disputed priority are explained inside entries. Credit includes named contributors and collective traditions. Superseded models remain visible for their historical role; useful approximations retain their domains of validity. Open questions and speculative proposals carry explicit labels.
Entries cite scholarly histories, origin: Entries cite scholarly histories, original research, textbooks, museums, and scientific institutions. Citations beside the introduction and history link claims to their supporting sources. Edge citations support the stated relationship or the ingredients of a conceptual inference. Guided tours are narratives through the atlas; consecutive stops do not imply a direct derivation.
Coverage includes natural and formal sci: Coverage includes natural and formal sciences and selected social sciences. The collection is an introductory, source-linked synthesis, not a substitute for specialist historical review. Its sources and interpretations can be revised as evidence improves.
